children: has risen above the single-family rental cap rate, creating what Reventure App CEO Nick Gerli described as a negative opportunity cost for buying investment properties.

Gerli said U.S. real estate investment had fallen 50% over the past four years, arguing that higher Treasury yields had changed the relative appeal of investment properties. He pointed to a 10-year Treasury yield of 5.1% versus a 4.8% cap rate for single-family rentals.

The accompanying chart from Reventure, using Zillow, FRED and Reventure calculations, showed the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.1% in September 2026, above the 4.8% cap rate. The chart labels the crossover as the first time in more than 20 years that the 10-year Treasury yield has exceeded the cap rate.

The gap marked a reversal from much of the period shown in the chart. From 2009 through the early 2020s, the single-family rental cap rate remained above the 10-year Treasury yield, although the spread narrowed and fluctuated over time. The two measures converged in 2025 and 2026 before the Treasury yield moved above the cap rate in September.

Gerli said the shift meant buying real estate for cash flow had a negative opportunity cost compared with buying government bonds, as investors could earn a higher stated yield from the 10-year Treasury than the rental cap rate shown in the chart.

He also said the number of people buying investment properties had fallen 50% over the past four years and argued that the change was having a significant impact on prices in some markets. Those figures were claims made by Gerli and are not directly quantified in the accompanying chart.

title: 10-year Treasury yield tops rental cap rate for first time in 20 years
